title: Padrino
notes: Padrino 0.16 on Sinatra with its ERB templates (which escape by default) and helpers, in production mode, on Puma with its default threads in one process.
details: A Padrino application laid out as padrino-gen makes it (config/boot.rb, config/apps.rb, app/app.rb with Padrino::Rendering and Padrino::Helpers, models/, app/views with a layout), with the shop added: /about and the item page are ERB views rendered by Padrino's renderer, which escapes what <%= %> prints unless it is marked safe (its SafeBuffer), with Padrino's number_to_currency for the price and link_to for the links; the API sets the JSON content type and returns the item as JSON. /about is rendered on each request, since Padrino has no build-time prerendering. Production mode (RACK_ENV), Padrino's logger sent to its :null stream so nothing is logged, and the framework's default middleware (Sinatra's Rack::Protection, method override, head) stays; no sessions and no compression, which are off by default. Started by the benchmark runner on one Puma server with Puma's own thread defaults and no workers, where padrino start would start the server itself. Gems are installed one at a time from gems.lock.json after their age and sha256 are checked; the padrino gem brings padrino-admin, -gen, -cache and -mailer, as a generated Gemfile does, though Padrino loads only the core and helpers here; puma and nio4r compile native extensions at install.
